attempts.evidence: Pass 1 — full 2000x2590 raster. Legend: red "overspeed:by_kmh=2.5 — mistake · failing (wide)", green "solved 34 km/h — ideal · good", both matching the manifest, including the `wide` outcome word (J1 pass). The green ideal carries the full auto marker set: an hourglass turn point low on the entry straight, an open ring apex late in the corner, a filled dot exit, and double-chevron release glyphs on the exit — all on the green line, and the red mistake carries none, which is exactly what `auto` means for a scene with no marks: field (ideal-role only). No glyph floats off a line (J2 pass, J7 pass). "wait for the radius to open" leads to the green apex ring and "too fast — pushed wide as it tightens" leads to the red line's run-wide detection station on the entry; both are anchored and legible (J3 pass). No occluders (J4 na). J5: the red line sits fractionally outside the green all the way through and the gap grows as the radius tightens, ending with the red arrowhead on the outer edge — a marginal overspeed progressively pushed off the tightening exit, drawn rather than asserted (J5 pass). At 2x everything is legible (J8 pass). J6 na, J9 na.

Pass 2 — SVG draw list against the manifest. Two polylines: bad #b32e2e / arrow-failing, good #1f6f43 / arrow-good, matching declared failing and good (J1 pass). data-marker-class inventory: {good, turn_point} x1, {good, apex} x1, {good, exit} x1, {good, release} x4 — every glyph on the ideal, none on the mistake, and the single apex confirms the ONE late apex the scene's note claims (J2 pass). No {bad, ...} entry anywhere, so the J2 finding that once put a red apex ring on this figure's overspeed line at its first metre has not returned (J7 pass). Two <text> callouts beyond the legend for the two declared labels (J3 pass). Zero rays, zero occluders (J4 na). data-terminal-reason="off_road" on bad only.

Pass 3 — close read of the marker vocabulary at 2x. The apex glyph is an OPEN ring with a visible hole and the exit glyph is a smaller FILLED disc; at this raster the two are plainly different marks rather than two dots of different sizes, which is the separation APEX_RING_STROKE_PX and EXIT_DOT_R exist to guarantee. The release glyphs read as paired chevrons, distinct from both. The proportion gate on this figure is `warn` rather than `fail`, and nothing in the drawing contradicts that — the corner fills the frame without the road being squeezed to a ribbon (J8 pass).
